Dataset name: Kasavakan Puyuma Noun Phrase Markers Dataset
normalized_task_category: Linguistic Theories, Cognitive Modeling, and Psycholinguistics
ai_dataset_relationship: Introduced
ai_content_evidence_type: Explicit target speech community / fieldwork provenance
ai_content_evidence_note: The dataset contains 377 sentences elicited from five Kasavakan Puyuma speakers. The paper explicitly locates the Puyuma community, including Kasavakan, in Taitung County in southeastern Taiwan.
ai_annotator_notes: Taiwan is supported through the explicitly identified speech community, not merely by mapping the Puyuma language to a country. The paper does not separately state the physical interview site.

ai_dataset_relationship: Reused
ai_content_evidence_type: Reused generic Wikipedia corpus; example-country mentions only
ai_content_evidence_note: WikiPassageQA is described as a reused Wikipedia-based collection. United States/USA and Sweden appear in qualitative example queries in Figure 2, not as dataset provenance or represented populations.
ai_annotator_notes: Deep review: reused dataset. The original WikiPassageQA paper (Cohen, Yang, Croft, SIGIR 2018) lists all creators at UMass Amherst, USA; the South Korea producer label corresponds to the MICRON paper authors, not the reused dataset creators. Dataset Link in the Atlas row also points to the MICRON repository rather than the original WikiPassageQA resource.

ai_dataset_relationship: Introduced; derived from GuessWhat?! images/objects
ai_content_evidence_type: Crowdsourced dialogue; participant country unspecified
ai_content_evidence_note: The new corpus contains 3,746 non-cooperative dialogues from native-English-speaking crowd participants, but the paper does not state their country. Images and goal objects are sampled from the original GuessWhat?! corpus.
ai_annotator_notes: All dataset creators are affiliated with the University of Pittsburgh, USA. The paper gives no independent U.S. provenance for the crowd participants or dialogue content.

ai_dataset_relationship: Reused
ai_content_evidence_type: Reused Reddit corpus; no country-specific population
ai_content_evidence_note: SARC is explicitly a reused corpus of 1.3 million self-annotated sarcastic Reddit statements with conversation context. The paper provides no evidence that India is the represented population.
ai_annotator_notes: Deep review: reused dataset. India is the current SarcEmp author's location. The original SARC paper (Khodak, Saunshi, Vodrahalli, LREC 2018) lists the creators at Princeton University, USA; SARC itself is a Reddit corpus rather than an India-specific dataset.

normalized_task_category: Information Extraction, Retrieval, and Text Mining
ai_dataset_relationship: Introduced; annotation layer over CNN/DailyMail
ai_content_evidence_type: Derived summarization corpus; annotator country unspecified
ai_content_evidence_note: TLHD-CNNDM is created by human token-level annotation of BART summaries generated from CNN/DailyMail test examples. The paper does not assign the underlying articles or volunteer annotators to Switzerland as a represented population.
ai_annotator_notes: The authors are at Idiap/EPFL in Switzerland; the paper says family, friends, and colleagues volunteered to annotate but gives no annotator-country provenance. Switzerland is therefore producer geography, not independently established content geography.

ai_dataset_relationship: Introduced; derived from multiple existing corpora
ai_content_evidence_type: Derived social-media/paraphrase corpora; crowdsourcing location unspecified
ai_content_evidence_note: ParaDetox is an English detoxification resource built from toxic sentences sourced from Jigsaw/Reddit/Twitter and from ParaNMT paraphrases, with Yandex.Toloka crowdsourcing. The paper does not establish Russia or Germany as represented populations.
ai_annotator_notes: Russia and Germany are the institutional locations of the dataset creators. Neither the source corpora nor Toloka worker locations are documented as Russia/Germany content provenance.

normalized_task_category: Information Extraction, Retrieval, and Text Mining
ai_dataset_relationship: Introduced; meta-dataset derived from NLP-progress and NLP papers
ai_content_evidence_type: Scientific-paper/leaderboard meta-dataset
ai_content_evidence_note: NLP-TDMS contains leaderboard annotations crawled from NLP-progress together with corresponding NLP papers. Italy is the conference location and Ireland is the authors' institutional location; neither is content provenance for NLP-TDMS.
ai_annotator_notes: Deep review: this is a meta-dataset and the paper also introduces ARC-PDN separately. The paper does not explicitly define one natural-language content language for NLP-TDMS, so I did not infer English from the publication language.

ai_dataset_relationship: Introduced; composite derived pretraining corpus
ai_content_evidence_type: Composite pretraining corpus; source/language geography is not population provenance
ai_evidence_source: 8.pdf: Appendix C.2 Details of Decorated Corpus; Table 3
ai_content_evidence_note: The Decorated Corpus is composed from Dolma, CC-CN, C4, The Pile, and Baidu-Wiki. The paper describes these as source corpora (including English and Chinese sources), not as evidence that China or the United States are represented populations.
ai_annotator_notes: Deep review: composite multi-source corpus. China is also producer geography (Tsinghua University and ModelBest, Beijing), but the U.S. label is likewise unsupported as represented-country provenance. The Atlas Dataset Link points to OpenFinData, which is used as an evaluation benchmark in the paper rather than being the Decorated Corpus source.

ai_dataset_relationship: Introduced; synthetic API query-response dataset
ai_content_evidence_type: Synthetic/self-instructed API queries; geographic examples are not provenance
ai_evidence_source: 9.pdf: Figure 3/§3.3 dataset construction; §4.1 API and Dataset Details
ai_content_evidence_note: The dataset is generated from seed queries, self-instruction, API execution, and reformatting across 26 APIs, with 1,000 GPT-4 query-response pairs per API. Country names such as UK/Germany occur in example weather queries, not as population provenance; China is not established as represented content.
ai_annotator_notes: The creators are at Zhejiang University, China. The Atlas Dataset Link points to Facebook Research's MaskFormer repository, one example external tool/model source, not to the paper's API query-response dataset.

normalized_task_category: Hierarchical Structure Prediction, Syntax, and Parsing
ai_dataset_relationship: Introduced; derived from published linguistic examples
ai_content_evidence_type: Japanese linguistic-example corpus; validator country unspecified
ai_content_evidence_note: JBLiMP is built from acceptability judgments extracted from journal articles on Japanese syntax and validated by native Japanese speakers through Lancers. The paper does not state participant/content country, so Japanese language identity or use of a Japanese platform cannot establish Japan as content provenance.
ai_annotator_notes: Japan is clearly producer geography (University of Tokyo), but the paper does not independently locate the extracted examples or crowd validators as a Japan-represented population. Flagged because the automated Japan label could plausibly come from either affiliation or language inference.

normalized_task_category: Speech recognition, text-to-speech, and spoken language understanding
ai_dataset_relationship: Introduced; speech layer built on Spider
ai_content_evidence_type: Explicit speaker-country provenance
ai_evidence_source: 11.pdf: §3 Dataset Construction and §3.2 Dataset Statistics; Figure 1(c)
ai_content_evidence_note: MASpider has 9,693 spoken utterances recorded by 11 speakers from six countries. Figure 1(c) labels Korea, China, Thailand, Japan, Britain, and American; AtlasNLP captured Japan/China/Thailand/United States but omitted Korea and Britain/United Kingdom.
ai_annotator_notes: The recordings themselves are English spoken questions with different accents. The paper does not say that Japanese, Chinese, Thai, or Korean are dataset languages; those are speaker-country/language-background attributes. Human reviewer should normalize the paper's labels 'Korea', 'Britain', and 'American' to the project country taxonomy.

ai_dataset_relationship: Reused (UD Telugu-MTG)
ai_country_set_error_type: No explicit country provenance; country inferred from Telugu context
ai_content_evidence_type: Language/community inference for reused grammar-book treebank
ai_content_evidence_note: The paper says Telugu is predominantly spoken in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana and later identifies the reused resource only as the Universal Dependency Telugu dataset. The dataset country is therefore not directly stated; India is a plausible language/community inference rather than explicit content provenance.
ai_annotator_notes: Official UD Telugu-MTG documentation says the treebank consists of grammar-book examples from Modern Telugu Grammar and was manually annotated by Taraka Rama (University of Oslo, Norway) and Sowmya Vajjala (Iowa State University, USA). It does not give a country provenance for the underlying example sentences. External check: https://universaldependencies.org/treebanks/te_mtg/index.html

ai_dataset_relationship: Introduced/expanded (IAC 2.0 extends IAC 1.0 with additional forum sources)
ai_country_set_error_type: No user-geolocation provenance; US inferred from topical/domain framing
ai_content_evidence_type: Country-specific topical/domain inference
ai_content_evidence_note: IAC 2.0 combines 4forums, ConvinceMe, and CreateDebate. The paper explicitly says 4forums covers topics relevant to the US political landscape and includes a gun-control subset from CreateDebate, but it does not geolocate forum users. United States is therefore plausible contextual inference, not direct participant provenance.
ai_annotator_notes: Because IAC 2.0 merges several online debate sources, the US interpretation should remain an inference rather than be treated as a directly observed country attribute for all posts.

normalized_task_category: Computational Social Science, Cultural Analytics, NLP for social good
ai_dataset_relationship: Introduced; Wikipedia-derived annotated biography corpus
ai_content_evidence_type: Biography target population contradicts proposed producer country
ai_content_evidence_note: WikiBio contains 20 Wikipedia biographies of African and African-American writers. Italy appears as an author/institution location, not as the stated provenance or represented population of the biography content.
ai_annotator_notes: The corpus spans multiple African/African-American biography subjects, so assigning a single replacement content country without inspecting all 20 biographies would require additional deep review. Italy should not be retained as content provenance.

ai_dataset_relationship: Reused (Words.hk Cantonese-English dictionary corpus)
ai_country_set_error_type: No explicit country provenance; inferred from Cantonese/Hong Kong-Guangdong context
ai_content_evidence_type: Source/dialect geography inference
ai_content_evidence_note: The paper describes Words.hk as an open Cantonese-English dictionary and frames Cantonese around Hong Kong, Macau, and Guangdong in southern China. It does not state a country for individual dictionary examples, so China is an indirect source/dialect inference rather than explicit content provenance.
ai_producer_country_verdict: Incorrect / cannot determine from reuse paper
ai_annotator_notes: The Manchester authors reuse Words.hk rather than create it, so United Kingdom should not automatically be treated as the producer geography of the specified dataset. Original Words.hk producer geography needs separate human verification. AtlasNLP's 'Chinese' label also loses the paper's explicit Cantonese distinction.
human_producer_country_verdict: Incorrect / cannot determine from reuse paper

ai_dataset_relationship: Extended/reused (Tuvan translation contribution to FLORES)
ai_country_set_error_type: Country inferred from Tuvan speech community, not original FLORES source-text provenance
ai_content_evidence_type: Speech-community/translator inference for translated benchmark
ai_evidence_source: 16.pdf: §1 Introduction, §3.1 Language Overview, and §4.1 Data Collection
ai_content_evidence_note: The paper states that Tuvan is an official language of the Republic of Tuva in Russia and that the FLORES Tuvan translation team consisted of native Tuvan speakers. The underlying FLORES sentences were sampled from Wikinews/Wikijunior/Wikivoyage, so Russia is best treated as inferred community provenance for this Tuvan extension, not as the geographic content of the source sentences.
ai_annotator_notes: The paper provides job roles rather than geographic affiliations for the authors. Russia for producer geography is therefore also an inference from the explicitly Tuvan translation team/community and should be human-checked.

ai_dataset_relationship: Introduced; derived from ICLR-2023 review-rebuttal forums
ai_content_evidence_type: Conference review-forum source with no country provenance
ai_content_evidence_note: RR-MCQ contains 196 review-revision multiple-choice questions constructed from 55 reviews of 14 ICLR-2023 papers. The source is an international peer-review forum; the paper provides no country provenance for the reviews, papers, or questions. China is the authors' affiliation geography.
ai_annotator_notes: Clear affiliation-as-content case; the dataset construction section does not support China as represented content geography.

ai_dataset_relationship: Introduced; semi-automatically generated from curated spatial-NLI patterns
ai_content_evidence_type: Synthetic pattern-generated data with no geographic population
ai_content_evidence_note: SpaceNLI examples are automatically generated from manually curated spatial inference patterns and lexical substitutions. Country/place names that appear in seed examples are semantic content examples, not dataset provenance. The Netherlands is the authors' Utrecht University affiliation.
ai_annotator_notes: Synthetic dataset; no meaningful content-country population is established by the paper.

ai_dataset_relationship: Introduced/expanded (GOOD.MA_v2 extends GOUD.MA)
ai_content_evidence_type: Explicit country-specific dialect and source-site provenance
ai_evidence_source: 19.pdf: Abstract/§1 and §3 GOOD.MA_v2 Dataset Description/Data Collection
ai_content_evidence_note: GOOD.MA_v2 is explicitly a Moroccan Darija summarization corpus expanded by scraping more than 50,000 articles from the GOUD.ma news website. The paper directly identifies Moroccan Darija as the target variety and GOUD.ma as the source.
ai_annotator_notes: The paper notes that titles are Moroccan Darija while article bodies are Modern Standard Arabic or a mix of MSA and Darija. AtlasNLP's generic 'Arabic' is broadly compatible but less specific than the paper.

ai_dataset_relationship: Reused (DravidianLangTech@NAACL 2025 shared-task dataset)
ai_content_evidence_type: Reused YouTube comments; language/regional inference plus affiliation leakage
ai_evidence_source: 20.pdf: §1 and §3 Dataset and Task Overview; original Rajiakodi et al. 2025 shared-task overview, pp.75-76
ai_content_evidence_note: The reuse paper says Tamil and Malayalam are South Indian languages and uses the shared-task dataset, but does not geolocate comments. The original shared-task overview says the data are YouTube comments scraped with targeted queries and likewise gives no commenter country. Bangladesh is the reuse-paper authors' affiliation; India is at best an inferred language/regional association, not direct provenance.
ai_annotator_notes: Deep review because this is a reused shared-task resource. The original overview paper lists dataset-team affiliations in India and Ireland and states Tamil/Malayalam are also spoken beyond India; it does not establish the YouTube commenters' country. Original source checked at https://aclanthology.org/2025.dravidianlangtech-1.115.pdf

ai_dataset_relationship: Introduced; composite/derived from seven Polish QA resources and existing multilingual resources
ai_country_set_error_type: Country inferred from Polish-language scope rather than geographic provenance
ai_content_evidence_type: Language/community inference; composite source provenance
ai_content_evidence_note: MAUPQA is explicitly a Polish QA dataset, but its seven components draw on Polish Wikipedia, the Polish subset of CCNet, machine-translated NQ, MKQA, multilingual FAQ data, templates, and Wiktionary. The paper does not establish Poland as the geographic origin of all underlying question/passage content, so Poland is a reasonable language-based inference rather than explicit content provenance.
ai_annotator_notes: Composite dataset: several components are translated or automatically generated from internationally scoped resources. Keep Poland as inferred content geography, not directly observed provenance.

normalized_task_category: Computational Social Science, Cultural Analytics, NLP for social good
ai_dataset_relationship: Introduced/extended web-crawled corpus for Brazilian Portuguese
ai_content_evidence_type: Explicit country-specific language variety / corpus scope
ai_content_evidence_note: The paper explicitly states that the resulting BrWaC resource is a large corpus for Brazilian Portuguese and applies its web-corpus construction framework to build that resource. Brazil is therefore directly supported by the stated variety and corpus scope.
ai_annotator_notes: The paper also experiments with English reference corpora, but the specified BrWaC dataset itself is the Brazilian Portuguese web corpus; English should not be assigned as a BrWaC dataset language.

ai_dataset_relationship: Reused (WMT News Crawl 2007); separate downstream Irish data comes from LoResMT21
ai_country_set_error_type: Overattribution / conflation of dataset languages with countries and of separate datasets
ai_content_evidence_type: Reused multilingual news corpus; no country-specific population provenance
ai_content_evidence_note: For WMT News Crawl 2007, the paper uses English and German 1M-sentence subsets. The Irish data is explicitly a different English→Irish COVID-19 dataset from LoResMT21. Thus Ireland is not provenance for the specified WMT News Crawl dataset, and Germany is at most an inference from the German-language subset rather than geographic content provenance.
ai_producer_country_verdict: Incorrect / cannot determine from reuse paper
ai_annotator_notes: AtlasNLP appears to have merged country/language information from two separate experimental resources: WMT News Crawl (English/German) and LoResMT21 (English/Irish). The WMT corpus creators should be checked separately if producer geography is needed.
human_producer_country_verdict: Incorrect / cannot determine from reuse paper

ai_dataset_relationship: Reused (SweLL-gold); paper derives a 69-sentence evaluation subset
ai_content_evidence_type: Explicit learner-corpus collection context from original SweLL provenance
ai_evidence_source: 24.pdf: §2.1 SweLL; original SweLL corpus paper (Volodina et al., 2016), pp.1-2
ai_content_evidence_page: 24.pdf PDF p.2; original SweLL PDF pp.1-2
ai_content_evidence_note: The reuse paper identifies SweLL-gold as essays by learners of L2 Swedish. The original SweLL corpus description states that learner metadata includes time of residence in Sweden and that the subcorpora were collected at Swedish educational institutions, including the University of Gothenburg and Stockholm University. Sweden is therefore supported by dataset provenance, not merely by the Swedish language.
ai_annotator_notes: Reused-dataset provenance was traced to the original SweLL description rather than relying only on the current University of Gothenburg affiliations.

ai_dataset_relationship: Reused (CORPUS-26 / MADAR parallel corpus)
ai_country_set_error_type: Multi-country set error: Oman omitted and United Arab Emirates added; Jerusalem mapping requires human resolution
ai_content_evidence_type: Explicit city-level dialect provenance
ai_content_evidence_note: CORPUS-26 is a commissioned translation corpus covering dialects of 25 named Arab-world cities. The city list explicitly includes Muscat (Oman) and contains no UAE city, so the proposed UAE attribution is unsupported and Oman is missing. The paper also includes Jerusalem as a city dialect; its country normalization is politically/geographically ambiguous and should be resolved by the human reviewer rather than guessed.
ai_annotator_notes: Deep multi-country review required. The original MADAR resource paper lists creator affiliations in Qatar, UAE, USA, and Bahrain, so AtlasNLP's producer set (Qatar, United States) is incomplete. Content-country list above intentionally leaves the Jerusalem country mapping unresolved rather than assigning it without an explicit paper-level mapping.

ai_dataset_relationship: Introduced (ArxivMIA)
ai_content_evidence_type: Academic-domain arXiv abstracts with no country-specific population provenance
ai_content_evidence_note: ArxivMIA contains Computer Science and Mathematics abstracts sourced from arXiv; member examples come from the arXiv subset of RedPajama and non-members are later arXiv abstracts. The paper does not define the benchmark as Chinese content or identify China as the provenance of the abstracts.
ai_annotator_notes: China matches the authors' Soochow University/OPPO affiliations, not the stated content provenance of the arXiv benchmark. The Atlas dataset link to zlib also does not correspond to the ArxivMIA release described in the paper.

normalized_task_category: Computational Social Science, Cultural Analytics, NLP for social good
ai_dataset_relationship: Introduced/curated from the National and University Library of Slovenia dLib archive
ai_content_evidence_type: Explicit national historical newspaper collection provenance
ai_content_evidence_note: The resource is explicitly a corpus of Slovenian historical periodicals, built from the dLib digital archive maintained by the National and University Library of Slovenia; the authors initially obtained roughly 250,000 periodicals published between 1771 and 1914.
ai_annotator_notes: The producer label United States is unsupported. The paper's creators are affiliated with institutions in Ljubljana, Slovenia and Vienna, Austria; upstream digitization was also performed by Slovenia's national/university library.

ai_dataset_relationship: Introduced (HILT); generated from NYTimes tweets and PolitiFact prompts with AMT annotation
ai_content_evidence_type: Mixed topical prompts from media/fact-checking sources; no fixed represented-country provenance
ai_content_evidence_note: HILT is generated from New York Times tweets and PolitiFact headlines and contains LLM-generated passages on varied topics and locations. Examples explicitly span places such as France, Turkey, India, the United Kingdom, the United States, and Ukraine. The paper does not define the dataset as content from the United States, India, and Bangladesh; those three countries instead match the authors' institutional affiliations.
ai_annotator_notes: Although the prompt sources are US-based organizations, source-organization location is not sufficient to assign a single content country to a globally topical synthetic dataset.

ai_dataset_relationship: Introduced; derived from HowStuffWorks articles with GPT-4-generated summaries
ai_content_evidence_type: General educational web content with no country-specific represented population
ai_evidence_source: 29.pdf: §3 Data Collection and Preprocessing; §6 The Dataset
ai_content_evidence_note: EduQuick consists of 500 educational articles scraped from HowStuffWorks across five broad topics and GPT-4-generated TikTok-style summaries. The paper does not identify Germany as the geographic provenance or represented population of the source content.
ai_annotator_notes: Germany is supported only as the authors' institutional location. HowStuffWorks publisher location likewise should not be substituted for the subject/content geography of the general educational articles.

normalized_task_category: Information Extraction, Retrieval, and Text Mining
ai_dataset_relationship: Reused/previously collected human-dialogue meeting corpus with document-reference annotations
ai_content_evidence_type: Explicit underlying newspaper/document provenance
ai_evidence_source: 30.pdf: §2.1 and §3 Description des données et des annotations
ai_content_evidence_note: The meetings discuss digitized front pages of francophone newspapers, primarily Le Monde (France), plus Le Soir (Belgium), Le Devoir (Québec/Canada), and La Presse (Tunisia). These are the actual documents the dialogue references are grounded in, so the four proposed content countries are directly supported by the corpus inputs.
ai_annotator_notes: The 22 meetings were recorded in a room at the University of Fribourg, Switzerland. The content-country labels correspond to the source newspapers, while Switzerland is producer/collection geography.

normalized_task_category: Information Extraction, Retrieval, and Text Mining
ai_dataset_relationship: Introduced; German-language biographical relation-extraction dataset compiled with guided distant supervision from Wikipedia/Wikidata/Pantheon
ai_country_set_error_type: Country inferred from German-language source corpus rather than geographic provenance of the biographies
ai_content_evidence_type: Language/community inference; source corpus is German Wikipedia, not a Germany-only population
ai_evidence_source: 31.pdf: Abstract; §3 Guided Distant Supervision (§3.1 Data Sources, §3.2 Automatic Labelling)
ai_content_evidence_note: The paper introduces a German biographical RE dataset and builds it from German Wikipedia text, Wikidata and Pantheon. Pantheon supplies biographies with multilingual Wikipedia presence. The paper does not restrict the people/events described to Germany, so Germany is plausible from the German-language corpus but is not explicit geographic content provenance.
ai_annotator_notes: Do not interpret German Wikipedia as a corpus of German people. The dataset creators are affiliated with the University of Luxembourg and Aston University (UK).

ai_dataset_relationship: Reused (DSTC2 & DSTC3); current paper performs SLU data augmentation/domain adaptation experiments on the challenge corpora
ai_country_set_error_type: Wrong country / affiliation leakage in reuse paper (China instead of United Kingdom)
ai_content_evidence_type: Explicit geographic domain provenance traced to the original DSTC challenge paper
ai_evidence_source: 32.pdf: §4.1 Data; Henderson et al. (2014), The Third Dialog State Tracking Challenge, §2.1-2.2
ai_content_evidence_page: 32.pdf PDF p.4; original DSTC3 PDF pp.1-2
ai_content_evidence_note: The reuse paper says DSTC2 contains restaurant-search dialogues and DSTC3 tourist-information dialogues. The original DSTC3 paper explicitly states that the dialogs involve people searching for restaurants, pubs and coffee shops in Cambridge, UK; DSTC2 is the Cambridge restaurant domain used for training. China is the current Shanghai Jiao Tong authors’ affiliation, not corpus geography.
ai_annotator_notes: Original DSTC3 authors/organizers were at University of Cambridge/VocalIQ (UK) and Microsoft Research Redmond (USA). The current China-based paper reuses the benchmark and should not determine producer geography.

normalized_task_category: Sentiment Analysis, Stylistic Analysis, and Argument Mining
ai_dataset_relationship: Reused (Corpus_500 from SentiALG); used here as the held-out Algerian Arabizi sentiment-analysis corpus
ai_content_evidence_type: Explicit country-specific dialect/corpus description
ai_evidence_source: 33.pdf: §5.1 Experimental Setup and §5.2 Experimental Results; cited SentiALG corpus paper
ai_content_evidence_note: The paper explicitly calls Corpus_500 “an Algerian Arabizi annotated corpus” and says its manual transliteration was performed by Algerian-dialect natives. Algeria is therefore directly supported, not inferred from author affiliation.
ai_annotator_notes: Corpus_500 is cited to Guellil et al. (2018), SentiALG. That paper’s authors span Algerian institutions and the University of Stirling (UK), so AtlasNLP’s UK-only producer set is incomplete.

ai_dataset_relationship: Introduced (ScholarlyRead); semi-automatically generated and manually checked QA over scientific-article abstracts
ai_content_evidence_type: General scholarly article source with no country-specific represented population
ai_content_evidence_note: ScholarlyRead is built from roughly 300 articles in two Elsevier Computer Science journals (Artificial Intelligence and Computer Networks), using article abstracts as contexts. The paper does not constrain the source articles to India. India matches the IIT Patna authors, not the content provenance.
ai_annotator_notes: The dataset is legitimately produced by the IIT Patna authors, but the international journal articles used as source documents should not inherit the producer country.

ai_dataset_relationship: Reused (USoMS); current paper annotates a subset of the German personal-narrative transcripts with emotion carriers
ai_content_evidence_type: Explicit original data-collection location plus German spoken-personal-narrative corpus description
ai_evidence_source: 35.pdf: Abstract and §3 USoMs Corpus; Rathner et al. (2018), State of Mind: Classification through Self-reported Affect and Word Use in Speech, Methods
ai_content_evidence_page: 35.pdf PDF pp.1,3; original USoMS paper PDF pp.1-2
ai_content_evidence_note: The reuse paper identifies USoMS as a database of spoken personal narratives in German. The original USoMS study states that the study took place at the Department of Clinical Psychology and Psychotherapy, University of Ulm, with data collected there in 2017. Germany is therefore explicit collection provenance.
ai_annotator_notes: AtlasNLP appears to use the current emotion-carrier paper’s Germany/Italy affiliations as producer metadata. USoMS itself was created by the original team at German institutions (Ulm/Augsburg) with Imperial College London (UK); Italy belongs to the later annotation paper.

ai_dataset_relationship: Reused (HatEval / SemEval-2019 Task 5); this is a participating-system paper
ai_country_set_error_type: Language-to-country overattribution; tweet/user geography is not established
ai_content_evidence_type: English- and Spanish-language Twitter data without explicit country/geolocation provenance
ai_evidence_source: 36.pdf: Abstract/§1; Basile et al. (2019) original HatEval task paper
ai_content_evidence_page: 36.pdf PDF p.1; original HatEval PDF pp.1-3
ai_content_evidence_note: HatEval contains English and Spanish Twitter messages about hate speech against immigrants and women. Neither the reuse paper nor the task description establishes the tweets/users as being from the United States and Spain. English≠United States and Spanish≠Spain for content-country provenance.
ai_annotator_notes: Original HatEval organizers/authors were based in Italy and Spain. The German affiliations in the current system paper are not dataset-producer geography. No reliable tweet-country labels were found.

normalized_task_category: Information Extraction, Retrieval, and Text Mining
ai_dataset_relationship: Introduced/expanded (MalwareTextDBv2.0); SemEval shared-task version extends the earlier MalwareTextDB
ai_content_evidence_type: Cybersecurity reports drawn from a global public repository, without Singapore-specific content provenance
ai_evidence_source: 37.pdf: §2 Data Description and Task Definition; §2.1.1 Data Collection
ai_content_evidence_note: MalwareTextDBv2.0 annotates 85 APT reports from the public APTnotes GitHub repository, selected from reports published in 2014-2015. The paper does not define those reports as Singaporean content. Singapore matches the SUTD authors/annotators.
ai_annotator_notes: Threat actors, victims, report publishers, and author institutions should not be conflated. No fixed content country is warranted from the shared-task paper.

ai_dataset_relationship: Introduced as a composite benchmark (ORCA) aggregating 60 public Arabic datasets across seven NLU task clusters
ai_country_set_error_type: Severe underattribution of a multi-country composite benchmark
ai_content_evidence_type: Explicit broad Arab-world coverage; country-level dialect task spans 21 Arab countries
ai_evidence_source: 38.pdf: §3.1 Benchmark Design and §3.2 Tasks/Task Clusters; NADI-2020 country-level dialect dataset documentation
ai_content_evidence_page: 38.pdf PDF pp.4,6; original NADI-2020 paper/table of 21 country labels
ai_content_evidence_note: ORCA explicitly states that it includes datasets from wide regions of the Arab world and contains a country-level dialect-identification task covering 21 countries. The 21-country NADI label set includes the countries listed here. AtlasNLP records only Egypt, Jordan, Saudi Arabia and Kuwait, so it misses most of the benchmark’s explicit geographic coverage. Because ORCA combines 60 datasets, component-level provenance can be even more nuanced than this country-label set.
ai_annotator_notes: High-value deep review: the manual country list is the explicit 21-country dialect task label set, not a claim that every one of ORCA’s 60 component datasets has exactly this provenance. A component-level union would require a separate benchmark-source audit.

ai_dataset_relationship: Introduced; topic-annotated standard-form-contract corpus from German and British-market online shops
ai_content_evidence_type: Explicit market/jurisdiction-specific source collection
ai_content_evidence_note: The authors crawl T&C links from two German price-comparison sites and their localized English versions targeted to the British market, then randomly select 142 German and 30 English T&C. Germany and the United Kingdom are directly supported by source-market provenance.
ai_annotator_notes: This is a strong explicit-provenance case: content countries are tied to the online-shop markets, not merely inferred from language.

ai_dataset_relationship: Introduced (ADPARAPHRASE); constructed from two Japanese ad-text datasets plus human/LLM paraphrases and preference judgments
ai_country_set_error_type: Country inferred from Japanese-language advertising context rather than explicit geographic source provenance

ai_evidence_source: 356.pdf: author affiliations and Abstract, p.1; §3/§5, p.3

ai_dataset_relationship: Reused SMD, CamRest, and MultiWOZ-2.1; added query annotations to the existing dialogue datasets.

ai_content_evidence_note: MiniLongBench is derived from LongBench and contains both English and Chinese tasks. China is plausible only indirectly from the Chinese-language subset; the paper gives no explicit country provenance for the benchmark as a whole.

Separate issue: the normalized task category 'Code Models' is too narrow for a benchmark spanning six task categories.

ai_dataset_relationship: Introduced GiCCS; derived from CROWDSS and BAS SmartKom dialogues with new BWS similarity annotations.

ai_evidence_source: 359.pdf: Abstract/§1, p.1; §3.1, p.3; §3.2 Data Annotation, p.4

Separate issue: normalized task category 'Dialogue and Interactive Systems' appears broader/misaligned; the paper's task is direct-speech sequence tagging.

ai_dataset_relationship: Introduced NLI4Wills, an NLI dataset generated from 23 publicly available legal wills with law and probate-condition inputs
ai_content_evidence_type: Explicit U.S. legal-document provenance
ai_content_evidence_note: The dataset uses U.S. Wills and Probates records and explicitly restricts the collected wills to Tennessee because including multiple states would require modeling different state laws. United States is therefore directly supported.

ai_dataset_relationship: Introduced TiconvQA, a Tibetan conversational reading-comprehension dataset with 20,358 dialogue turns built from 2,120 Tibetan passages
ai_content_evidence_type: Explicit China-based source ecosystem and Tibetan resource context
ai_content_evidence_note: TiconvQA is built from Tibetan materials sourced from Yongzin Encyclopedia and China Tibet Network; the paper also explicitly situates Tibetan as a minority language in China. China is independently supported by the source ecosystem rather than only the authors' affiliations.
ai_annotator_notes: Country evidence comes from the named Chinese/Tibetan source platforms and resource scope.

ai_dataset_relationship: Curated a PolitiFact claim/evidence set for explanation refinement and evaluated explanations with American human participants
ai_content_evidence_type: Explicit U.S. political-news and participant scope
ai_content_evidence_note: The study uses PolitiFact claims described as spanning U.S. political news and evaluates explanations with American questioners/participants. United States is directly supported.
ai_annotator_notes: Producer geography is under-attributed: the paper includes Taiwan-based Academia Sinica/NTHU/NTU affiliations and a Pennsylvania State University affiliation in the United States.

ai_dataset_relationship: Reused and digitized a large Ancient Greek literary corpus to train/fine-tune BERT for authorship attribution of Plutarch and Pseudo-Plutarch texts
ai_content_evidence_type: Historical Ancient Greek corpus with no defensible modern Germany/Portugal content provenance
ai_content_evidence_note: The data consist of Ancient Greek texts from digital classics repositories. Germany and Portugal are current-author institutional locations, not the geographic provenance of the historical textual content. A modern-country mapping for the ancient corpus is not established by the paper.
ai_annotator_notes: The master language field is blank although the paper explicitly trains on Ancient Greek. The master task label Code Models is also not a good description of the authorship-attribution/language-modeling task. Historical-to-modern country normalization should be human-adjudicated rather than guessed.

ai_dataset_relationship: Introduced LexAbSumm, an aspect-based legal summarization dataset built from ECtHR judgments and ECtHR press-service fact sheets
ai_content_evidence_type: Pan-European ECtHR legal-case corpus with heterogeneous respondent-state content
ai_content_evidence_note: LexAbSumm is sourced from European Court of Human Rights jurisprudence and thematic ECtHR fact sheets covering many cases and alleged violations. The paper does not define the dataset as German content; Germany instead matches the authors' Technical University of Munich affiliation.
ai_annotator_notes: A complete case-by-case respondent-state mapping would require deeper extraction from ECtHR metadata; the proposed single-country Germany label is unsupported.

ai_dataset_relationship: Introduced GUNSTANCE, a labeled and unlabeled Twitter stance dataset centered on banning/regulating guns after U.S. mass-shooting events
ai_content_evidence_type: Explicit U.S. political-event/social-media provenance
ai_content_evidence_note: The paper explicitly states that GUNSTANCE contains tweets collected during seven mass-shooting events in the United States and targets the U.S. gun-control/regulation debate.
ai_annotator_notes: Producer set is incomplete: authors are affiliated with Kansas State University and University of Illinois Chicago (United States) and University Politehnica of Bucharest (Romania).

normalized_task_category: Speech recognition, text-to-speech, and spoken language understanding
ai_dataset_relationship: Reused the Nijmegen Corpus of Casual French (NCCFr), selecting speech from 44 speakers for speaker-classification and occlusion experiments
ai_content_evidence_type: Explicit upstream speaker and recording geography
ai_content_evidence_note: The current paper reuses NCCFr. The original corpus documentation states that speakers were recruited in Paris, raised in Central/Northern France, and recorded at ILPGA in Paris. France is therefore independently supported, not merely inferred from French or current-author affiliations.
ai_annotator_notes: Current paper alone gives limited geographic detail, but the cited upstream NCCFr resource establishes France clearly.

ai_content_evidence_type: Explicit participant residence/population geography
ai_content_evidence_note: The paper states that DAIC participants are drawn from populations living in greater Los Angeles: the general public and veterans of the U.S. armed forces. United States is explicit.
ai_annotator_notes: The New Orleans proceedings location is unrelated to content provenance.

ai_dataset_relationship: Reused EmpatheticDialogues; manually annotated about 500 response intents and automatically analyzed the full approximately 25K-dialogue dataset
ai_content_evidence_type: Explicit U.S. crowdsourced participant geography

ai_annotator_notes: The current authors are at EPFL in Switzerland, while the reused dialogue population is explicitly U.S.-based.

normalized_task_category: Multimodality and Language Grounding to Vision, Robotics and Beyond
ai_dataset_relationship: Introduced EMPATHICSTORIES++, a 53-hour multimodal longitudinal empathy dataset from 41 participants interacting with in-home social robots
ai_content_evidence_type: Explicit U.S. deployment geography
ai_content_evidence_note: The dataset comes from month-long in-home deployments, and the paper explicitly states that the deployment was conducted across the United States.
ai_annotator_notes: Country evidence is explicit in the deployment description and independent of the MIT affiliation.

ai_dataset_relationship: Introduced a custom 1,200-sample Indian Sign Language gesture dataset across 12 classes, paired with an ISL-to-Odia mapping for translation
ai_content_evidence_type: Explicit Indian data-collection and ISL/Odia scope
ai_content_evidence_note: The paper explicitly says the 1,200 gesture samples were captured under diverse Indian backgrounds and builds the system around Indian Sign Language and Odia for use in India/Odisha.
ai_annotator_notes: All listed authors are affiliated with IIIT Bhubaneswar, Odisha, India; South Korea is unsupported as producer geography. The master language field omits Indian Sign Language, which is the gesture-side language of the dataset.

ai_dataset_relationship: Introduced a bias-aware English instruction-tuning corpus derived from selected AskX subreddits for geographic, political, age, and gender groups
ai_content_evidence_type: Explicit demographic/national-group corpus design
ai_content_evidence_note: The geographic bias groups explicitly include German data from AskAGerman and American data from AskAnAmerican. The corpus also contains broad Latin American and Middle East regional groups, which are not safely expandable into individual sovereign countries without participant-level geography.
ai_annotator_notes: Deep review retained only for country-normalization policy: two additional geographic groups are regions (Latin America and Middle East), not individual countries.

ai_dataset_relationship: Introduced LIST2QA, generated from unlabeled customer-support documents in ConditionalQA and MultiDoc2Dial with new list-grounded QA instances
ai_content_evidence_type: Explicit source-document jurisdiction/platform provenance
ai_content_evidence_note: LIST2QA uses UK public-welfare documents from ConditionalQA for train/validation/test data and also uses MultiDoc2Dial public support documents such as ssa.gov and va.gov for additional unseen-domain test samples. The proposed United Kingdom label therefore misses the U.S. source component.
ai_annotator_notes: Kyung Hee University supports South Korea for the explicitly geolocatable producer affiliation; the paper gives AWS AI Labs without author-location addresses, so no additional producer country is asserted here.

ai_evidence_source: 375.pdf: Abstract; §3 Vietnamese Ground Truth Data Collection
ai_content_evidence_note: The study explicitly targets Vietnamese native speakers, making Vietnam a plausible community-based attribution, but the actual participants are described as Vietnamese students studying in Australia. However, the Twitter users are labeled by language rather than residence/nationality, so the four country assignments are defensible language-community inferences rather than direct participant geolocation.

The original TRAC corpus states that Facebook/Twitter data were collected from pages/issues expected to be discussed among Indians and describes the source as popular social-media platforms in India. India is therefore the supported content geography.

ai_dataset_relationship: Introduced the OUD Search Dataset of 2,893 YouTube search results (1,776 unique videos) from 73 opioid/treatment queries, with expert and synthetic myth labels

ai_content_evidence_note: The paper frames the study around the U.S. opioid epidemic and Appendix A.1 explicitly states that Google Trends was configured to focus on the United States when selecting topics and search queries. The resulting OUD Search Dataset is therefore U.S.-grounded.

ai_dataset_relationship: Collected verbal-memory story-retell speech through a mobile assessment application from 105 psychiatric patients and 120 healthy undergraduate participants, then transcribed and modeled the retells.

ai_annotator_notes: Producer geography is under-attributed: authors are affiliated with U.S. institutions and with the University of Tromsø/Norwegian Centre for eHealth Research in Norway.

Dataset name: WMT21 News and Biomedical Shared Translation Tasks
ai_dataset_relationship: Reused WMT21 constrained-track parallel and monolingual corpora for English↔German and English↔Russian news translation and English↔Russian biomedical translation.
ai_content_evidence_type: Language-based country inference; no country-specific corpus provenance established
ai_content_evidence_note: The paper establishes English, German, and Russian WMT corpora, not country-specific data from Germany, Russia, and the United States. Germany and Russia are at most plausible language-community inferences; United States is unsupported as content geography and coincides with the producer location.
ai_annotator_notes: Do not equate WMT language pairs with verified national provenance. The U.S. label appears to come from NVIDIA's Santa Clara affiliation rather than the translation data.

ai_dataset_relationship: Introduced SCILEAD, a manually curated scientific-leaderboard dataset containing exhaustive task-dataset-metric-result annotations from 43 NLP papers and 27 leaderboards.

ai_content_evidence_note: SCILEAD consists of scientific publications and leaderboard annotations; the paper does not define the underlying scientific content as German. Germany instead corresponds to producer affiliations in Darmstadt/Berlin.
ai_annotator_notes: Country attribution to Germany is not supported by dataset provenance.

ai_dataset_relationship: Reused NPN-Cooking as a downstream entity-tracking benchmark and additionally pre-trained on more than 2.5 million English recipes gathered from several internet recipe datasets.
ai_content_evidence_type: Recipe-domain corpus without country-specific provenance
ai_content_evidence_note: NPN-Cooking is described as an English recipe-domain entity-tracking dataset, and the pretraining recipes come from internet recipe resources. No Indian content provenance is established; India is the authors' institutional location.
ai_annotator_notes: The country field appears to conflate the IIT Kharagpur producer location with recipe content.

normalized_task_category: Computational Social Science, Cultural Analytics, NLP for social good
ai_dataset_relationship: Introduced an annotated dataset of place-name inscriptions from early-modern Japanese ukiyo-e landscape prints and used it for named-entity recognition and distant viewing.
ai_content_evidence_type: Explicit cultural-object and geographic provenance
ai_content_evidence_note: The dataset consists of inscriptions on Japanese ukiyo-e prints depicting Japanese places/topography and is drawn from a Japanese-print database at Ritsumeikan University, Kyoto. Japan is explicit.
ai_annotator_notes: Japan is supported by the artifact and place-name provenance, independent of the Greece/Sweden producer affiliations.

ai_dataset_relationship: Introduced LegalAFSum, an extractive legal summarization dataset created by collecting legal documents from the United Kingdom and Singapore and having law students annotate summaries and legal terms.
ai_content_evidence_type: Explicit legal-document source-country provenance
ai_content_evidence_note: The paper explicitly states that it collected 468 legal documents from two countries, the United Kingdom and Singapore, before constructing LegalAFSum.
ai_annotator_notes: The proposed two-country content set is directly supported in the dataset-construction appendix.

ai_dataset_relationship: Constructed and annotated a corpus of 415 narrative essays written in Chinese by high-school students for sentence-level discourse-mode identification and essay-scoring analysis.
ai_content_evidence_type: Student/language-community inference rather than explicit collection-location provenance
ai_content_evidence_note: The paper explicitly says the essays were written by Chinese high-school students in their native Chinese language, but it does not independently state the students' residence or the data-collection country. China is plausible from the speech/education community but remains indirect.
ai_annotator_notes: Following the audit rule, Chinese-language/student-community evidence is treated as an inference rather than verified country provenance.

ai_dataset_relationship: Introduced two survey datasets in which high-school students and MeteoGalicia meteorologists drew polygons for geographic descriptors in the context of Galicia.
ai_content_evidence_type: Explicit survey-site and geographic-task provenance
ai_evidence_source: 389.pdf: §2 The resource and its interest; Acknowledgments
ai_content_evidence_note: The task is explicitly grounded in Galicia in northwestern Spain; the student survey was run at a high school in Pontevedra and the expert survey with the Galician Weather Agency.
ai_annotator_notes: Producer geography omits the Universidade de Santiago de Compostela (Spain) and University of Malta affiliations. The survey descriptors were presented in Spanish; English appears as translations in the paper rather than as collected participant-language data.

ai_dataset_relationship: Constructed Dataset V4 for SNOMED CT concept encoding by integrating English textual descriptions and mappings from multiple public medical ontologies, classifications, vocabularies, and linked-open-data resources.
ai_content_evidence_type: International ontology/terminology resources without country-specific content provenance
ai_content_evidence_note: Dataset V4 is generated from SNOMED CT and multiple public/linked medical knowledge resources (ICD, MeSH, MONDO, ORDO, UMLS, etc.). The paper does not define the data as Bulgarian or U.S. content; those countries correspond to author affiliations.
ai_annotator_notes: Producer geography is also under-attributed because one author is explicitly affiliated with MIT in the United States in addition to the Bulgarian institutions.

ai_dataset_relationship: Introduced M-QALM, a standardized benchmark aggregating 22 existing clinical/biomedical QA datasets across multiple-choice and abstractive QA.
ai_content_evidence_type: Multi-dataset benchmark with several country-specific examination sources
ai_content_evidence_note: The paper explicitly highlights licensing-exam questions from India and Spain, and M-QALM also includes USMLE, which is explicitly a U.S. medical licensing exam. The proposed India/Spain set therefore omits at least the United States; other component datasets may add further provenance.
ai_annotator_notes: Producer metadata over-attributes South Korea and the United States; the title page lists AICS/NUS in Singapore and the University of Manchester in the UK. Exact content-country normalization across all 22 component benchmarks merits human adjudication.

ai_dataset_relationship: Introduced ASSET, a crowdsourced English sentence-simplification corpus containing 23,590 simplifications for 2,359 TurkCorpus source sentences, with multiple rewriting transformations.
ai_content_evidence_type: Explicit annotator-residence provenance
ai_content_evidence_note: AMT workers were explicitly required to be residents of the United States, United Kingdom, or Canada. The proposed three-country set is directly supported.
ai_annotator_notes: Country provenance is unusually clear because worker residence was an explicit qualification requirement.

ai_dataset_relationship: Created 3K and 10K Korean user-to-user scheduling-dialogue datasets from consented real dialogues plus crowdsourced conversations under controlled age, gender, relationship, and task conditions.
ai_content_evidence_type: Korean-language/community inference; participant residence not stated
ai_content_evidence_note: The paper explicitly says the collected dialogues are in Korean but does not state that the users reside in South Korea. South Korea is therefore plausible but indirect rather than verified content provenance.
ai_annotator_notes: Producer metadata omits Samsung Research India Bangalore. The South Korea content label should remain Inferred rather than Correct.

normalized_task_category: Information Extraction, Retrieval, and Text Mining
ai_dataset_relationship: Collected a corpus of 20,058 English obituaries from The Daily Item, Remembering.CA, and The London Free Press, then annotated obituary sections for automatic zoning.
ai_content_evidence_type: Explicit publication/source geography
ai_content_evidence_note: The paper explicitly states that The Daily Item contains U.S. obituaries, Remembering.CA covers Canada, and The London Free Press covers London in the UK.
ai_annotator_notes: All three proposed content countries are directly tied to named obituary sources.

ai_dataset_relationship: Reused the SHROOM shared-task dataset for semantic-hallucination detection across definition modeling, machine translation, and paraphrase generation.
ai_content_evidence_type: Multi-source/multilingual NLG benchmark with no U.S.-specific provenance
ai_content_evidence_note: SHROOM draws definitions, paraphrases, and MT parallel corpora from multiple sources and language pairs. The paper does not establish the United States as dataset provenance; U.S. appears in an example sentence rather than as the collection geography.
ai_annotator_notes: The master language field is blank. SHROOM includes English definition/paraphrase material and multilingual machine-translation material; this system paper does not enumerate the complete MT source-language inventory.

ai_dataset_relationship: Introduced SimQG by sampling about 500 SQuAD question-passage pairs, generating questions with three QG models, and collecting human judgments from AMT workers.
ai_content_evidence_type: Explicit annotator-location provenance
ai_content_evidence_note: The paper explicitly required SimQG AMT crowdworkers to be located in the United States. Singapore is the producer affiliation, not the human-annotation provenance.
ai_annotator_notes: This is a clear producer/content swap: NUS is in Singapore, while the SimQG annotators were explicitly U.S.-located.

ai_dataset_relationship: Reused a company-provided corpus of 8,439 Thai-language complaints annotated into nine complaint categories for neural complaint classification.
ai_content_evidence_type: Thai-language and local-source inference; complaint-user geography not explicitly stated
ai_content_evidence_note: The corpus is explicitly Thai-language and was provided/verified by Feedback180 Co., Ltd., but the paper does not state where the complainants were located. Thailand is a strong language/community inference rather than explicit user provenance.
ai_annotator_notes: Producer metadata omits the multiple Thailand-based affiliations and retains only Japan.

ai_dataset_relationship: Introduced MESAQA by transforming the healthcare-oriented MASH-QA dataset into multi-span abstractive, evidence-grounded QA instances using LLM generation/filtering and expert validation.
ai_content_evidence_type: Reused healthcare QA source with no Taiwan-specific content provenance
ai_content_evidence_note: MESAQA is built from MASH-QA and is primarily healthcare/medical. The paper does not establish Taiwan as the provenance of the underlying contexts or questions; Taiwan corresponds to the authors' affiliations.
ai_annotator_notes: Country attribution appears to be producer-affiliation leakage from NTU/Academia Sinica.

ai_dataset_relationship: Constructed synthetic quality-estimation training data from WikiMatrix mined Wikipedia bitext for English–German and English–Chinese, evaluating against corresponding human-annotated QE data.
ai_content_evidence_type: Language-based inference from German and Chinese Wikipedia bitext
ai_evidence_source: 399.pdf: §3 Approach to Data Synthesis; §4 Experimental Setup
ai_content_evidence_note: The data are defined by English–German and English–Chinese language pairs mined from Wikipedia, not by national provenance. Germany and China are plausible language-community mappings but are not explicitly established as source countries.
ai_annotator_notes: Following the audit rule, language→country mapping is retained as Inferred rather than marked automatically Incorrect.

normalized_task_category: Multimodality and Language Grounding to Vision, Robotics and Beyond
canonical_language_string_cleaned: English; Chinese; French; German; Italian; Arabic; Polish; Hungarian; Bulgarian; Croatian; Serbian
ai_dataset_relationship: Introduced EXAMS-V, a 20,932-question multilingual multimodal benchmark built by retracing official state-exam PDFs from EXAMS and adding Chinese Gaokao and English JEE Advanced exam questions.
ai_content_evidence_type: Explicit multi-country school-exam provenance
ai_evidence_source: 400.pdf: §3 EXAMS-V Dataset; §3.1 Data Collection and Analysis; upstream EXAMS source description
ai_content_evidence_note: EXAMS-V is explicitly assembled from exams from multiple national education systems. The paper directly adds Gaokao from China and JEE Advanced from India, and states that parallel exams come from Croatia and the UAE. The inherited EXAMS resource also explicitly contains state-exam material from Hungary. Thus the proposed UAE/Bulgaria pair is far from exhaustive; exact source-country normalization for every inherited language subset requires deeper review.
ai_annotator_notes: Producer metadata incorrectly adds South Korea; the title page lists MBZUAI in the UAE and Sofia University in Bulgaria. The content-country field needs human review because EXAMS-V inherits a multi-country state-exam resource and the current paper does not enumerate every source country in one place.
